title: Underwriting Guide: One Cardinal Rental Reimbursement Option per Vehicle
content:
**Rule.** Cardinal Rental Reimbursement is held per vehicle. A vehicle carries at most one option at a time. A customer may hold an option on every vehicle that carries physical damage, and the product sets no cap of its own on how many vehicles a customer may cover. An option can be added to a vehicle only when no option on that vehicle is active or suspended.

## Points of judgement

- **Records decide.** Whether an option already sits on the vehicle is read from the vehicle's rental option records and their status. What the customer remembers about the vehicle does not decide it.
- **The vehicle is the unit.** The check looks only at options on the same vehicle that the new option would cover. An option on another vehicle of the household plays no part in it.
- **Statuses that block.** An option with status *active* or *suspended* on that vehicle blocks a new one. An option with status *removed* is neither active nor suspended, so it does not stand in the way under this rule.

## Status of an existing option on the same vehicle

| Existing option on the same vehicle | Does this rule block another option? |
|---|---|
| None | No |
| Active | Yes |
| Suspended | Yes |
| Removed | No |
| An option on a different vehicle | Not considered |

## Examples (hypothetical households)

1. A household has three vehicles. Two carry physical damage and one is insured for liability only. This rule allows an option on each of the two vehicles with physical damage. Holding two options does not reach a per-customer cap, because the product sets none.
2. A vehicle's option was suspended while its physical damage was in storage. The customer asks for a second option on that same vehicle. The suspended option blocks it.
3. A vehicle's earlier option shows status removed. This rule does not prevent a new option on that vehicle.
